config.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form

intro.title: Form Validation with Zod + React Hook Form
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple user registration form with real-time validation. You'll learn how to use Zod, a schema declaration and validation library, to define the rules for your form fields. Then, you'll integrate Zod with React Hook Form to manage the form's state, handle submissions, and display validation errors. By the end, you'll have a working form that validates user input like email format and password strength before submission.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for any application requiring robust user input, such as sign-up forms, checkout flows, or data submission panels in dashboards. For example, a user settings page where email, password, and profile details must be validated before saving, or a financial dashboard where transaction filters require strict date and number formats. Implementing Zod with a form library ensures data integrity and user-friendly error feedback, preventing invalid submissions and reducing backend errors in real-world scenarios like e-commerce or admin tools.

objectives: Initialize a Vue component with a form using the Composition API
Configure a form schema with Zod to define validation rules
Integrate Vue Form with Zod using the vee-validate library
Bind form inputs to reactive state with validation rules
Manipulate form submission to handle validation results
Render validation error messages conditionally based on form state
Control form reset functionality to clear validation states

steps.title: Import Vue, ref, and required validation libraries
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref from 'vue', zod from 'zod', and the required @vee-validate libraries for form validation.
steps.hint: You'll need to import Vue for the component, ref for reactive state, zod for schema validation, and @vee-validate libraries for form handling.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing multiple dependencies
import { ref } from 'vue'
import { z } from 'zod'
import { useForm, useField } from 'vee-validate'

steps.expectedOutcome: All necessary dependencies are imported at the top of the file.
successCriteria: Vue, ref, zod, and @vee-validate libraries are imported correctly.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some dependencies, but check if you're missing any from the instruction.

steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'FormValidationExample' with a setup function and a template section that returns a div wrapper.
steps.hint: Use the Vue 3 Composition API with the setup function. The component should return a template with a single root div element.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue, ref, zod, and @vee-validate libraries here

// Create your Vue component here

successCriteria: The component is named FormValidationExample, includes a setup function, and has a template that returns a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your component is named FormValidationExample, includes a setup function, and has a template with a div element.

steps.title: Define the Zod validation schema
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a Zod schema object named 'formSchema' with validation rules for three fields: name (required string), email (required string that must be a valid email), and password (required string with minimum 8 characters).
steps.hint: Use the z.object() method from Zod to create your schema. Each field should be defined with z.string() and chain validation methods like .min(1) for required and .email() for email validation.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Zod schema object named 'formSchema' is defined with validation rules for name, email, and password fields.
successCriteria: The 'formSchema' object is created using z.object() and contains three fields: name, email, and password, each with appropriate validation rules.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a schema, but it's missing some validation rules or fields. Make sure to include all three fields (name, email, password) with appropriate validations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The schema definition is incorrect or missing. Remember to use z.object() to create a schema object with three fields, each with appropriate validation rules.

steps.title: Initialize form state with ref
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, create a reactive form state object using ref with three properties: name, email, and password, all initialized as empty strings.
steps.hint: Use ref to create a reactive object containing the form fields.
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive formState object is created with name, email, and password fields, each starting as an empty string.
successCriteria: A formState variable is declared using ref, containing name, email, and password properties all set to empty strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref to create the reactive object and that it includes all three required fields (name, email, password) as empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form state wasn't properly initialized. Remember to use ref to create a reactive object with name, email, and password properties, all starting as empty strings.

steps.title: Set up form validation with useForm
steps.instruction: In the setup function, call useForm with the Zod schema to initialize form validation.
steps.hint: Use the useForm hook from vee-validate and pass the Zod schema using toTypedSchema.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useForm hook is called with the Zod schema, connecting validation to the form.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling useForm and passing the schema with toTypedSchema.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form validation setup is incomplete. Use useForm with the Zod schema via toTypedSchema.

steps.title: Create the form structure in template
steps.instruction: In the template section of your Vue component, add a <form> element with @submit.prevent to prevent default form submission.
steps.hint: The form element should wrap the input fields you'll add later. Use @submit.prevent to handle form submission without page reload.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example form structure in Vue template
<template>
  <form @submit.prevent="handleSubmit">
    <!-- Form fields will go here -->
  </form>
</template>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a basic form structure in its template with proper form submission handling.
successCriteria: A <form> element exists in the template with @submit.prevent attribute to prevent default submission.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a form element, but it's missing the @submit.prevent attribute to prevent default form submission.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure isn't properly set up. Make sure you've added a <form> element in the template with @submit.prevent.

steps.instruction: Inside the template's form, add an input field for the name with v-model binding to formState.name.

steps.expectedOutcome: The form template now includes a text input bound to the name field in formState.
successCriteria: Input element for name is added inside the form
v-model binding to formState.name is present
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Display validation errors
steps.instruction: Add error message display for the name field using the validation results from useForm.
steps.hint: Use the errors object returned by useForm to display validation messages. In Vue template, you can access errors.name and conditionally show it.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: displaying validation error
{{ errors.name }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The name input field will have validation error messages displayed when validation fails.
successCriteria: A div or span element conditionally displays errors.name when present, using v-if or similar directive.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're displaying the actual error message from errors.name and using conditional rendering to only show it when there's an error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation errors aren't being displayed correctly. Check that you're accessing errors.name and using v-if to conditionally show the error message.

successCriteria: A function named handleSubmit is created that prevents default form submission and logs formState values.
